note: Every point is a recorded observation with the file it came from. Segments are solid only where the before/after record shows nothing was extended in between; dashed only from the last observation to a known expiry ledger. Nothing is drawn past an expiry. Remaining ledgers are endsAtLedger minus the observation ledger — derived at build time, never stored here.

series.label: guinea-pig B · instance
series.role: The control. Deployed 5 September, calibrated once that day with a disclosed extend, then left alone — and it expired on 21 September, as intended. Six measured readings run into the expiry; nothing extended it at any point.

series.label: guinea-pig A · instance
series.role: The watched one. Its decay was arranged by raising the alert threshold above its remaining TTL; the response was not. Each upward step names its actor and transaction.

steps.note: +1,000 ledgers requested; expiry +1,002 including inclusion delay. Fee charged 5,064 stroops.

Alert threshold raised to 1,500,000 so the engine would act — arranged timing, genuine response. Fee charged 44,725 stroops. No row here is labelled scheduled cron: as far as the record goes, the production cron has never extended anything.

series.label: shared code entry
series.role: One entry all three contracts depend on — A, B and C were built from one Wasm. Due to be extended at W3-D18-02d; touching it touches both decay proofs, which is why the write guard refuses it by key.
